public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1126

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1126](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1126)
- [Er60c] Erdős, P., *Problem 310*. Colloq. Math., 311.
- [dB66] de Bruijn, N. G., *On almost additive functions*. Colloq. Math. (1966), 59-63.
- [Ju65] Jurkat, Wolfgang B., *On Cauchy's functional equation*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1965), 683-686.
-/

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory

namespace Erdos1126

/--
If
$$f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$$
for almost all $x,y\in \mathbb{R}$ then there exists a function $g$ such that
$$g(x+y)=g(x)+g(y)$$
for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x)=g(x)$ for almost all $x$.

Proved independently by de Bruijn [dB66] and Jurkat [Ju65].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 26 28, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1126.lean"]
theorem erdos_1126 : answer(True) ↔ ∀
    (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (h :
      ∀ᵐ (p : ℝ × ℝ) ∂(volume.prod volume),
        f (p.1 + p.2) = f p.1 + f p.2),
    ∃ h : ℝ → ℝ,
      (∀ x y, h (x + y) = h x + h y) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂volume, f x = h x) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1126

reformulations.difference: The source's 'for almost all x,y ∈ ℝ' is written as `∀ᵐ (p : ℝ × ℝ) ∂(volume.prod volume), f (p.1 + p.2) = f p.1 + f p.2`. Here `volume` is Mathlib's Lebesgue measure on the Borel σ-algebra, not its completion. `f` is not assumed measurable, so the exception set may be non-measurable. Likewise 'f(x)=g(x) for almost all x' is `∀ᵐ x ∂volume, f x = h x`. A reader might worry that the Borel (uncompleted) measure, or a non-measurable exception set, changes the meaning.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `∀ᵐ` is defined through the outer measure: it says the exception set has outer measure 0. That is the same as lying inside a measurable (Borel) null set. I proved this in Lean for both the hypothesis and the conclusion, using `ae_iff` and `exists_measurable_superset_of_null`. Subsets of Borel null sets are exactly the null sets of the completed Lebesgue measure. So the hypothesis is Jurkat's 'almost all pairs (x, y) in the sense of plane measure (Lebesgue)', and the conclusion is his 'coincides with f(x) for almost all x in the sense of linear measure'. `(volume : Measure (ℝ × ℝ)) = volume.prod volume` holds by `rfl`. A non-additive function (the indicator of {0}) satisfies the hypothesis, so the statement is not vacuous.

reformulations.difference: erdosproblems.com states the result as a theorem ('If … then there exists …'), not as a question. The Lean wraps it as `answer(True) ↔ ∀ f, … → ∃ h, …`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `answer(True)` elaborates to `True`, and `True ↔ P` is equivalent to `P`. I checked this in Lean against the declaration's own type with `Iff.of_eq (true_iff _)`. `answer(True)` is also the right polarity: the source records the problem as 'solved in the affirmative'.

review.notes:
No findings and no status issues. The file matches erdosproblems.com/1126 word for word. Jurkat's Theorem I (PAMS 1965) fixes the reading of 'almost all x, y' as planar Lebesgue measure, which is what `volume.prod volume` gives. Status agrees with the source: `research solved`, `answer(True)`, and a `formal_proof` link, against 'PROVED (LEAN): solved in the affirmative'.

The `formal_proof` link (plby/lean-proofs, blob/main, v4.29.1): its `Erdos1126.erdos_1126` is literally the file's right-hand side. Under this repo's Lean v4.33.1 one step failed: a `simpa` that closed an `∀ᵐ` goal in v4.29.1 now needs a preceding `rw [MeasureTheory.ae_iff]`. With that one-line patch the proof compiles here and gives the full `True ↔ …` statement. `#print axioms` lists only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The link points at a branch rather than a pinned commit; that is only a metadata nit.

Side remarks, none a defect:
- The module docstring's [Er60c] citation (Erdős, Problem 310, Colloq. Math. 7 (1960), 311) is confirmed by Jurkat's reference list. The erdosproblems page itself now lists only [Ju65] and [dB66], after a forum report that [Er60c] would not load.
- Jurkat also proves uniqueness and allows f to be defined only almost everywhere. The erdosproblems statement asks for neither, and the Lean follows erdosproblems.
- de Bruijn's argument, as formalized, uses only the iterated consequence (for a.e. x, for a.e. y). So the result would also hold under the weaker iterated reading; the planar reading in the file is the standard one, and Jurkat states it explicitly.
- de Bruijn's paper is only available as a scanned PDF without a text layer, so I could not read its wording. The erdosproblems text and Jurkat's theorem were enough to settle the statement.
- erdosproblems.com blocks direct curl requests (Cloudflare), so I read its pages through the r.jina.ai reader proxy.
- AMS 39 (functional equations) would also fit alongside 26 and 28; this is not a defect.
